## What was built

Added four implementation files (the provided `csv_spec.mbt`, `specs/`, and `*_pub_test.mbt`/`csv_qc.mbt` were left untouched):

- `csv_scanner.mbt` — a bounds-checked `Cursor` over the decoded `Array[Char]`, with `peek`/`at_end`/`advance` and `consume_terminator` (treats CRLF as one terminator, plus lone LF/CR). All input indexing lives here, so the parser cannot read past the end and never panics.
- `csv_parser.mbt` — the single-pass state machine: `parse → parse_record → parse_field → parse_quoted_field / parse_unquoted_field / after_quoted_field`, plus `check_field_count` for the rectangular-record rule. `parse(input : StringView) -> Doc raise` is the entry point.
- `csv_printer.mbt` — `print(doc : Doc) -> String`, exact inverse of `parse` over parse's image, quoting only where the dialect requires it (empty fields, or fields containing `,`, `"`, CR, LF).
- `csv_parse_error.mbt` — `pub suberror ParseError` (`UnterminatedQuote`, `QuoteInUnquotedField`, `TextAfterClosingQuote`, `InconsistentFieldCount`) with a `message` renderer.

Behavior follows `specs/csv.md`: LF/CRLF/CR boundaries; `""` escaping; embedded commas/newlines preserved; empty input → zero records; a single trailing terminator adds no record; a blank line is one record with one empty field; no trimming; and rejection of unterminated quotes, quotes in unquoted fields, text after a closing quote, backslash escapes, and ragged records.

## What was built

Four focused source files (all well under the 1000-line limit), plus docs and tests:

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| [scanner.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/ini_run_1/scanner.mbt) | Line splitting (LF/CRLF), trailing-backslash counting, inline-comment cutting |
| [value.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/ini_run_1/value.mbt) | Quoted parsing, per-carrier escape tables, unquoted continuation joining |
| [parser.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/ini_run_1/parser.mbt) | Line classification, section headers, entries, `parse` |
| [printer.mbt](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/ini_run_1/printer.mbt) | `print` with value escaping and section-name protection |

The required root-package API `@ini.parse(input : StringView) -> Doc raise` and `@ini.print(doc : Doc) -> String` are implemented, with `Doc` unchanged.

## Key behaviors

- **Lines**: LF/CRLF, blank lines, `;`/`#` full-line comments; a final line break doesn't create a phantom continuation target, so a dangling marker errors.
- **Sections**: `[name]` up to the first `]`, trimmed, one wrapping quote pair stripped, nested `[` rejected, only trailing whitespace after `]`; repeated headers re-open; line-based recognition never fires inside a value.
- **Entries**: first `=`/`:` splits; key trimmed, non-empty, no control chars; later separators are value text.
- **Values**: quoted carriers close on the same line; inline comments require a preceding whitespace; each carrier decodes its own table and keeps other backslashes (`C:\Program` is itself).
- **Continuations**: odd trailing backslash run joins the next raw line directly (whitespace before the marker kept); even run is escaped literals; only the first line owns syntax, later lines are plain text.
- **`print`**: global first, then sections; values always double-quoted with escapes; a section name that `parse` would trim/unquote is emitted inside an extra quote pair so it round-trips.

- Added tests: `ini_edge_test.mbt` (separators, trimming, comments, escape tables, the full continuation run-length table, CRLF, malformed inputs, an exhaustive parse↔print round-trip over ~2,400 hostile values, section-name round-trips) and `ini_real_test.mbt` (git-config, systemd, php.ini shapes).

- An independent worktree audit confirmed criteria (2)–(7) hold under adversarial probing and flagged one round-trip gap for padded/quote-wrapped section names, which I fixed in `printer.mbt`.

Architecture (root `ini` package):
- error.mbt — private IniError(line, message)
- scanner.mbt — LF/CRLF splitting, trailing-backslash runs, whitespace/inline-comment predicates

## What was built

## Key correctness points

- **Streaming**: every multi-byte value loops over `Reader::read` across partial reads; end of stream inside a value (including a key, a packed payload, a group) raises.
- **Varints**: ten-byte limit, non-minimal encodings accepted, bits beyond the 64th dropped, an eleventh continuation byte raises; writers are minimal.
- **32-bit readers** consume the whole varint (still detecting overflow) and keep the low 32 bits; `int32`/`enum` sign-extend on write; `sint*` zigzag.
- **Length prefixes** are validated as full 64-bit values, so `2^32` is rejected even though its low 32 bits are small; payloads are read in bounded 4 KiB chunks so a bogus length cannot force a huge allocation before the short stream raises.
- **Strings** are strictly UTF-8-validated (overlongs, surrogates, >U+10FFFF, truncation, stray continuations rejected; U+FEFF kept).
- **Packed fields** decode through a `LimitedReader`; mid-element truncation raises; the outer reader resumes exactly after the payload.
- **`read_unknown`** skips all wire types, including nested groups, and raises on mismatched group ends, bare EGROUP, and wire types 6/7.
- The reader types are opaque (`pub struct` with private fields), matching the declared abstract types; the explicit `extend` makes the trait-method attachment idiomatic.

## What was built

Implementation (root `uri` package, split by responsibility):

- `rfc3986_uri.mbt` — `Uri::parse` and `Uri::to_string`
- `rfc3986_parser.mbt` — scheme detection and `[userinfo@]host[:port]` parsing
- `rfc3986_validate.mbt` — character classes + the per-component whitelist validator
- `rfc3986_ip_literal.mbt` — IPv4 / IPv6 / IPvFuture / zone-id host-literal validation
- `rfc3986_resolve.mbt` — Section 5.2 resolution, path merge, and dot-segment removal
- `rfc3986_scan.mbt` — total, bounds-checked scan helpers
- `rfc3986_error.mbt` — the `UriError` suberror
- `uri_extra_test.mbt` — additional RFC-derived conformance tests
- `README.md` — architecture, approach, usage, testing, and design rationale

Key behavior: components are stored still percent-encoded (`None` = absent, `Some("")` = present-but-empty), IPv6/IPvFuture brackets are kept, only the scheme is lowercased, splitting is delimiter-first (`#`, then `?`, then scheme, then `//`) so inner delimiters are never misread, and resolution implements Section 5.2/5.2.3/5.2.4 literally (verified against every Section 5.4.1 and 5.4.2 example, including `http:g` strict mode). Validation rejects forbidden raw characters (space, `<>`, `\`, `^`, backtick, `{}`, `|`, controls), malformed percent-encodings, invalid schemes, non-numeric ports, malformed IP literals, and ambiguous authorities (stray `@`/`:`, stray brackets, junk after a literal). Scanning is code-unit based and slicing clamps, so parsing is panic-free on arbitrary input.
